question_text:
A hypothetical metal is known to have an electrical resistivity of $3.3 \times 10^{-8}(\Omega-\mathrm{m})$. A current of 25 A is passed through a specimen of this metal 15 mm thick. When a magnetic field of 0.95 tesla is simultaneously imposed in a direction perpendicular to that of the current, a Hall voltage of $-2.4 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~V}$ is measured. Compute the following:
(a) the electron mobility for this metal
(b) the number of free electrons per cubic meter.
Give your answer a tuple: (answer to (a), answer to (b)).The unit of the answer is ($\mathrm{m}^2 / \mathrm{V}-\mathrm{s}$, $\mathrm{m}^{-3}$).
response:
## Reasoning

**Hall effect relations:**

The Hall coefficient is
$$R_H = \frac{V_H d}{I B}$$

where $d$ is the specimen thickness (along the field direction). For a single-carrier metal,

$$R_H = -\frac{1}{n e}, \qquad \mu_e = \frac{|R_H|}{\rho}, \qquad \sigma = \frac{1}{\rho}=n e \mu_e$$

**Numbers:**
- $\rho = 3.3\times10^{-8}\ \Omega\cdot\text{m}$
- $I = 25\ \text{A}$, $d = 0.015\ \text{m}$, $B = 0.95\ \text{T}$
- $V_H = -2.4\times10^{-7}\ \text{V}$

$$R_H = \frac{(-2.4\times10^{-7})(0.015)}{(25)(0.95)} = -1.516\times10^{-10}\ \text{m}^3/\text{C}$$

**(a) Mobility:**
$$\mu_e = \frac{|R_H|}{\rho} = \frac{1.516\times10^{-10}}{3.3\times10^{-8}} \approx 4.6\times10^{-3}\ \text{m}^2/\text{V·s}$$

**(b) Electron concentration:**
$$n = \frac{1}{|R_H|e} = \frac{1}{(1.516\times10^{-10})(1.602\times10^{-19})} \approx 4.1\times10^{28}\ \text{m}^{-3}$$

$$\boxed{(4.6\times10^{-3},\ 4.1\times10^{28})}$$
